reviewer_summary.question: Why must a chosen word go through processing before choosing another word, and which earlier calculations can a cache preserve?
reviewer_summary.takeaway: Choosing blue uses is’s finished number; blue still needs its own pass, while each layer can reuse earlier keys and values because appending blue cannot change their inputs.

findings.problem: The bridge previews a whole chain of new operations at once and the picture still labels the new calculation as practice.

resolution.note: Bridge now leaves the completed practice case, shows actual inputs, and starts only the next preparation. No advance dump of the unknown recipe.

findings.problem: Scoring multipliers appear before their operands or use and may be mistaken for input lookups.

resolution.note: Remove the multiplier-list beat. Show the finished is number multiplied by the assigned factor, then identify the resulting candidate score and choosing-rule role.

findings.problem: Individually narrated repeated three-source decimals displace the purpose.

resolution.note: Apply the same parallel operation-row representation already used at the other repeated reads; all inputs and results remain visible.
